title: "Reliability"

There are many empirical estimates of reliability, but there is only one shared conceptual definition that informs all procedures: 

>...the consistency of scores across replications of a testing procedure [@aera_apa_ncme_2014]

## Error

Reliability, at its core, is fundamentally concerned with errors. These errors are really no different in occurrance than errors that occur in other aspects of life. For example, if you are at a pub and order a pint of beer, it is reasonable to expect a bit more or less than exactly 16 fl oz by the time it arrives at your table. Taps are notoriously imprecise machines. Bartenders are even more notorious for being generous, stingy, inattentive, or otherwise distracted. Any of these factors are reasonable factors that could result in your "pint" being an actual 15.87, 16.01, etc fl oz. Souses have a tolerance for this inexactitude with beer pours. Psychologists also need to acknowledge inexactitude with scores that arise from Psychological assessment responses.
